text:
Monica (oncall): FYI seeing a sudden latency and error spike for the continuous-batcher in us-west-2, started ~10m ago. 95th token latency > 6s and a handful of host OOMs.
incident-bot: ALERT: perf degradation detected on service=continuous-batcher cluster=us-west-2 severity=high triggered=1766601234
Monica (oncall): attaching logs from one affected pod. Paging churn and repeated CUDA pagefaults.
Sasha: noted, which stack? prefetch/kvcache growth or request-side batching?
Monica (oncall): looks like prefetch growth. kvcache size trending up steadily, then node started thrashing and kubelet killed container with OOMKilled. snippet: ```2026-03-15T12:04:02Z runtime: GPU OOM on allocation ctx=0x7f...
[continuous-batcher] prefetch_kv_bytes=1.9GB prefetch_items=23456
2026-03-15T12:04:04Z WARNING: page fault on GPU: SIGBUS````
Rami: customer impact? any 5xx spikes or user-facing sessions affected?
Support Ops: we see elevated 503s for AcornHealth production, rolling backlog increments on API route /v1/generate. Dashboard shows request queue growth correlating with batcher backlog.
Cheng: can you confirm node flaps? I see two nodes in the pool went NotReady and restarted around the same time. Possibly driver crashes.
Monica (oncall): correct. node-cc-047 and node-cc-053 both had dmesg GPU errors then kubelet restart.
Tala (eng-sre): initial triage: continuous-batcher's prefetch loop didn't backpressure properly when kvcache memory crosses threshold — growth -> larger batches -> more KV prefetch -> OOM -> node flap. Likely a deadlock in the placement/evict path.
Sasha: immediate mitigations: (1) throttle incoming traffic to continuous-batcher route; (2) switch routing policy to fallback model variant (smaller KV) for high-latency customers; (3) cordon+drain the flappy nodes.
Monica (oncall): executing throttle: applying rate-limit via envoy: ```rbac: route: /v1/generate -> rate_limit: 60rps```
deploy-bot: applied traffic control to route /v1/generate in cluster us-west-2 by user=Monica at 1766601302
Monica (oncall): cordoning node-cc-053 now to prevent churn while we patch. ```kubectl cordon node-cc-053 && kubectl drain node-cc-053 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -o yaml```
Rami: good. Any on-call config we can flip quickly? There's a runtime knob prefetch_kv_max_items and kvcache_eviction_threshold in ~/deploy/configs/continuous-batcher.yaml. We can set prefetch_kv_max_items=2000 to cap growth.
Cheng: I can push a hotfix config to the private control plane for Dedicated and Hosted runtime in us-west-2: set prefetch_kv_max_items=2000, prefetch_backpressure_ms=50, enable_immediate_eviction=true. Will do a canary to 10% first.
Sasha: canary + restart only for scheduler pods on unaffected nodes. Keep replicas so we don't reduce capacity too much.
Monica (oncall): oncall handoff incoming in ~20m; will leave instructions.
Tala (eng-sre): add a temporary sentinel that kills any batcher process when kvcache > 2GB to avoid node-level OOMs. Better than kernel-level GPU crash.
Rami: agree. Also enable runtime debug metrics to see per-request prefetch sizes, add alert if growth rate > 100MB/min.
Support Ops: customer comms: AcornHealth impacted ~10% of requests in the last 12m. Sent initial note to customer success to inform them we're mitigating and will follow up.
Cheng: pushing config change as a patch to staging now, will promote to canary. ```kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_KV_MAX_ITEMS=2000 PREFETCH_BACKPRESSURE_MS=50 --namespace=prod````
deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/continuous-batcher -> revision 2026.03.15-ht1 by Cheng at 1766601420
Monica (oncall): monitoring logs: after canary up, one instance reported immediate drop in kvcache growth. latency dropping to ~1.2s p95 on canary traffic.
Tala (eng-sre): still seeing one crash loop on older pods with prefetch enabled; that's expected until they get replaced. Keep an eye on GPU driver events.
Rami: if driver is unstable on those nodes, we should fully cordon and replace nodes rather than restarting containers repeatedly. Node restarts mask hardware issues.
Cheng: agree. cordoning node-cc-047 and opening replacement ticket with infra to repro driver SIGBUS with vendor drivers.
Monica (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (Cheng taking over): - mitigation: rate-limit applied, canary config deployed to 10% (PREFETCH_KV_MAX_ITEMS=2000), nodes cordoned: node-cc-053 drained, node-cc-047 cordoned pending replacement. - customer impact: AcornHealth 503s for ~20min, partial degraded service. - next steps: finish canary -> promote to 100% if stable for 10m, add sentinel eviction, coordinate infra for node replacement, follow up on driver debug logs.
Cheng: acknowledged, I'll take lead. leaving link to quick checklist and runbook snippets: ```# runbook excerpt
1) throttle via envoy route
2) set PREFETCH_KV_MAX_ITEMS
3) enable immediate_eviction
4) cordon/replace nodes with SIGBUS logs
5) monitor /metrics for kvcache_growth_rate
```
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to medium at 1766601745 after canary shows stability.
Support Ops: posting update to customers and CS: short blip, mitigation in progress, follow-up tomorrow with RCA.
Sasha: follow-up items for postmortem: - root cause analysis of non-backpressured prefetch loop - add e2e test simulating sustained kvcache growth - add auto-eviction guard - consider batching cap per-request to avoid runaway batch size.
Monica (oncall): leaving final note before handoff: if you see GPU pagefaults restart drivers only if infra confirms healthy; otherwise leave node drained and replace. Handing to Cheng. :white_check_mark:
